1h09:
Accounting is a vital and fascinating part of today’s global economy. Studying it at Hertfordshire brings students face to face with current trends, practices and concepts – not just within accountancy itself, but in the wider world of business.

This BA (Hons) Accounting degree is a highly practical, relevant course. It gives students the sought-after skills, latest academic theory and real-world experience they need to become a confident, knowledgeable, forward-thinking graduate with exceptional career prospects.

This course explores the role of accountancy in businesses of all sizes and forms, opening students' eyes to the diverse range of potential career paths ahead. It’s a multi-disciplinary, globally focused accounting degree, developed with innovative industry-leading companies and respected professional bodies.

At Hertfordshire, students will be taught by their team of leading academics, who together have created a supportive, inspiring learning environment. They’re joined by visiting industry specialists who bring with them years of real-world accounting experience and a real enthusiasm for sharing their insights with students.

This degree course offers exemptions from a range of accounting bodies including the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA), Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) and Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW).

Between the second and third year, students can do an entire year abroad at one of the partner universities based in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia. That means plenty of places for learners to go and explore. Students can also do a year’s work placement abroad or in the UK.
1h0b:
For those who are curious about financial matters within companies or want to kick-start their career with professional accreditations before they've even left university, then BA (Hons) Accounting and Finance is the course for them.

This degree course offers exemptions from a range of accounting bodies including the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA), Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) and Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW).

In the  first year, students will learn the principles of accounting and the basic mix of knowledge and skills they would require for a successful career in accounting. They'll explore financial information within companies and corporations and learn to analyze it. There is a dedicated module focusing on professional skills, such as communication and IT-literacy. Learners will investigate the different sides of business and where their role as an accountant sits within these.

In the second year, students' accounting knowledge and skill will be developed and so will their employability. They’ll focus on financial reporting, management accounting and financial management. They’ll also learn methods of enquiry and problem solving to ensure they are ready to go out into the real world. This will give them an advantage when they start working.

In the final year, students will build on the foundation they have established in their first and second years but will also challenge the knowledge they have gained in those previous years so that they can influence change in their future career. Students will take modules on advanced financial reporting and management accounting. They’ll also have the chance to pick from options such as research methods, taxation, Islamic finance and banking or information systems.

Between the second and third year, students can do an entire year abroad at one of the partner universities based in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia. That means plenty of places for learners to go and explore. Students can also do a year’s work placement abroad or in the UK.
1h0k:
BA (Hons) Architecture empowers students' to satisfy the requirements of a brief and re-energize our environment. Students will learn the technical knowledge to inspire their professional portfolio. They'll be taught how to analyze, develop, test and communicate their ideas.  Students will be working on drawings and models for domestic, public and commercial projects, such as houses, museums and cityscapes.  Be creative.

Learners can spend time in Hertfordshire's fantastic studios and workshops. There are woodworking, metalworking and casting workshops to help students develop real-world skills.  Students can try their hand at ceramics (for building facades), printmaking and life-drawing classes to enhance their sketching skills. Moreover, learners can make use of specialist computer software suites and even download software onto their personal laptop. With 3D printers, laser cutters, a welding booth and studio space at their fingertips, students can bring their ideas to life.

The Year Abroad will provide students in Creative Arts with the opportunity to expand, develop and apply the knowledge and skills gained in the first two taught years of the degree within a different organizational and cultural environment in a partner academic institution. Moreover, an optional 'Sandwich' placement year may be undertaken between the levels 5 and 6. Students undertake the placement within a commercial, public or not for profit setting that is able to provide an appropriate learning experience related to the creative and cultural industries.

The BA (Hons) Architecture is ARB (Architects Registration Board) prescribed and RIBA (Royal Institute of British Architect) validated course for Part I, based on its course content (including education aims, learning outcomes and assessment criteria); and evidence that the University has adequate resources in place to maintain and increase the achievement of pupils to standards required.
6aob:
This program is developed hand in hand with leading companies, an all-rounder course which is a perfect launchpad to kickstart a student's corporate management career or be an innovative business leader.

Students will be exposed to the heart of the latest challenges dominating businesses today such as sustainability, leadership, digital innovation and organisational psychology.

Students will get to explore practical business essentials such as global business environment, finance, marketing, technology and management behavior with options to delve deeper into areas that interest you.

Students will graduate with a well-rounded professional skillset, having learnt how to communicate, present and work with people, building your confidence and improving your CV.
1h11:
Program Description

A business degree is a powerful, career-launching qualification, and for those interested in a career in business, combining two subjects will give them sought-after skills, exciting experiences and a whole world of future career opportunities.

This degree gives students an in-depth understanding of today’s business world. They'll explore accounting, marketing and human resources, as well as the fast- moving international financial sector – from financial markets and investments to banking and economics. It’s an ideal choice for students who know they’d like a respected business degree and they’re interested in finance but perhaps not yet sure where they’d like to specialise. It enables students to bring both disciplines together, and to understand how they interact and impact on society.
1h2d:
Careers in event management and tourism are full of possibilities, with exciting projects in interesting places, all over the world. Whether students want to organize festivals and sports fixtures or develop thriving tourist destinations, degree program in Event Management and Tourism will help them launch a really successful career. It uses the latest theories and real- world case studies to explore their successes and failings, as well as their sustainability, impact, cultural attributes and community engagement.

BA (Hons) Events and Tourism Management is a multi disciplinary, globally focused course developed in collaboration with business leaders and professional bodies and taught by Hertfordshire’s highly regarded, experienced academics. It's recognised by the Tourism Management Institute (TMI) and is a key partner of the Association of British Travel Agents (ABTA)

Students will get to study real world case studies and broaden their horizons through the study abroad programme in second year with one of the partner universities in Europe, North America or Australia. Some combine their language study options with a half-year of study in the language home country and then a further half-year work placement in the same country. Without a doubt, they come back with excellent skills in a second language in addition to fantastic memories, experiences and career skills.

Students also have the opportunities to enhance their study and CV with a work placement sandwich year. It’s a chance to explore career possibilities, make valuable contacts and gain sought after professional skills.
1h3d:
Program Description

Join the next generation of media professionals, with a powerful, practical course that gives students the skills and agility to thrive in a rapidly changing industry. Explore the nature of language, communication and the media. Write news, features and fiction. Study films, music and celebrity. Design magazines, websites and a fascinating, successful future.

The media world is evolving fast. Digital and social media are developing at breakneck speed and changing the way we talk to, learn from and understand each other. At Hertfordshire, their mass comms course focuses on communication and media practice, encouraging students to be entrepreneurial and professional, with a diverse set of sought-after creative skills.

Students will have a whole range of opportunities, including exploring publishing and PR, examining the ethical and legal aspects of journalism, developing their voice as a writer, studying the context behind films, spending a life-changing year abroad or taking a year-long work placement.
1h3h:
In today’s fast-paced media world, people with the ability to write, design and harness new technologies are in high demand.

Studying the BA Media and Communications degree will equip students with a portfolio of practical skills as well as a theoretical and critical understanding of Media. This industry-focused approach, combining theory and practice, will help build their confidence, give them the communication and technological skills required for the industry and help them plan their career.

Students will learn how to design their own app proposal, build and edit brilliant websites and create a hard-hitting ad campaign, including PR. They’ll also learn what makes a good news story or feature, and how to write one. Using industry standard software and equipment, professionally-experienced academics and researchers will help students develop skills across divergent platforms and for different audiences.

These hands-on skills will be underpinned by an understanding of the global media industry, and the legal and ethical contexts of students' work. In the first year students will explore Global Media and Society, looking at who owns the news, at the influence of the BBC and commercial entities such as Sky and Murdoch’s News Corporation, and consider issues such as fake news.

Other core modules (courses) include introductions to Media Communications and Visual Communications – how to use text and graphics to reach key audiences – while students will gain technical skills through Photoshop or animation projects.

In the second year students will learn key research methods and skills including how to conduct interviews and run focus groups, and how to pitch to different client groups. Students will explore radio journalism and social media, while a module on App Design will help them understand the commercial potential for their ideas.

For students that are into music, film, food or travel, they'll have opportunities to create magazine layouts and pdfs for online publications on whatever subject interests them. A video option will give them the chance to create a brand for a product or service.

In the final year students will develop and refine their ideas and skills further. Whether they're keen to work in web design, social media, customer relations, PR or advertising, the skills they’ve gained will prepare them to be tomorrow’s creative entrepreneurs, confident in using different platforms to get ahead in their chosen career.
4p6u:
Program Description

MArch Architecture & Urbanism is a Masters of Architecture award within the Design programme at the School of Creative Arts. Within the programme there is strong emphasis on professional practice and the real-world applications of design. Students will develop key research skills and gain a good understanding of the work of other practitioners in their field.

The aim of the postgraduate programme is to equip students with the skills, knowledge and understanding required to practice at an advanced level, to foster their creativity and enhance their employment opportunities. Students will work alongside artists and designers who are involved with a wide variety of media and forms and will benefit from visiting architects and design professionals. Induction, seminars and social events for students and staff mean that they will be part of a friendly and supportive postgraduate community, which also includes film makers, musicians and professionals working in new media. Senior research staff and internationally renowned artists work with postgraduate students, helping students to develop original and challenging work.
6dv9:
The Master of Arts Public Relations with Digital Communications with Advanced Research a two-year course, where students will learn core principles and gain an advanced understanding of public relations and digital communications. The first year of this course is the same as the one-year The MA Public Relations and Digital Communication Course .It is the second year that differentiates these courses.

This MA Public Relations and Digital Communications course will enable students develop an understanding of the challenges in the PR and communications industry and apply the knowledge from the course to identify effective solutions to real-life case studies.Feel confident and prepared to work in the industry. This course incorporates theoretical and practical learning styles to equip student for a career in the field. This includes traditional lectures as well as workshops, masterclasses and online study.

Continuously develop and advance student PR and communication skills.Student will familiarise with media planning, writing for the press, reputational management and how to strategically analyse data to measure the impact of digital campaigns and more.Challenge thoughts and learnings to an advanced level, ensuring student are always open-minded and accepting of different perspectives that will positively influence the way student handle different PR situations.

Explore the public relations industry and trends of today, taught to student by our experienced staff, authentic coursework assignments, and expert speakers.
1h5l:
The MA Early Childhood Education programme supports learners in developing their knowledge and understanding of issues and practice through enquiry and research. It provides a range of module choices, but students are encouraged to bring their own ideas and focus on their respective professional interests.

Hertfordshire is ranked 1st as best university provider for Teacher Training in the UK (NSS). Students can greatly benefit from University's strong partnerships with over 300 schools and training providers across Hertfordshire, London, Bedfordshire, Buckinghamshire, and Cambridgeshire.

This MA Early Childhood Education award aims to equip students to enhance service provision at nursery, local and national level becoming or preparing to become a change agent in their own practice and in early childhood practice in general. Students will build on and deepen their knowledge and understanding of practice and theory in relation to child development, curriculum design and pedagogical leadership.

Taught sessions are built around discussion, discovery, shared learning and peer review with tutor support and expertise immediately at hand. Moreover, learners have access to the University’s Learning Resource Centre (LRC) and virtual learning environment.

Previous graduates have become successful practitioners within early years settings, as well as progressing onto further study and research.
6dvb:
The Advanced Research award offers students the opportunity to study an area of personal interest in depth to develop expertise in a chosen aspect of education. It is aimed at applicants who intend to pursue careers in senior leadership of education institutions, educational policy development, administration, and academic research. The course will also prepare students for progression into doctoral study.   The course is established for teachers and education practitioners who want to develop expertise and theoretical understanding of the field.

It is also for newly qualified practitioners looking to upgrade their qualifications and enhance their knowledge. Also for students who have had some experience in an aspect of educational practice which and would like to develop for future career development.

MA Education has Placement Year, a one-year course and Advanced Research pathways.
1h64:
The MA Games Art and Design degree meets the need of the gaming industry. This industry has developed dramatically from the days of the solo practitioner to become a global market where large teams of artists work in unison to create content for the next generation of interactive game technologies.

This course supports students who want to specialize in areas such as character design, hard-surface modelling, environment design or lighting and texturing as well as those who want to be generalists. The University supports all the standard software packages used in the industry and is constantly updating the range of technical instruction it offers. The MSc award fuses technical knowledge of real-time rendering with the aesthetic decisions and traditional skills learners will need as game artists.

On this course, students will also explore thinking about the cultural resonance of their work and about the audiences it is made for, about the nature of creativity, and the role of the cultural industries in a modern knowledge economy. Enquiry, research and clear communication being key elements that underpin this course.

Induction, seminars and social events for students mean that while studying and after they graduate, they'll be part of a friendly and supportive postgraduate community, which includes film makers, musicians and professionals working in other areas of creative media. Senior research staff and internationally renowned professionals also work with postgraduate students, helping them to develop an original individual approach.

The University of Hertfordshire is ranked 1st in the UK as Top Games Development School (10th worldwide) and 1st for Games Design & Development Production Excellence (Rookies World School Rankings® 2020). There are work related learning opportunities on this course, all students complete a live external brief provided by a major games studio as part of their coursework.

The MA Games Art and Design graduates work for most major gaming companies including BAFTA winning UK games studio Creative Assembly, Frontier, Splash Damage, Guerrilla Games, Epic Games and Rare.
95vy:
The Master of Business Administration with Extended Professional Practice is designed to provide students with a critical understanding of core business and management principles, including people management, marketing, and financial proficiency. The programme supports the development of strategic leadership capabilities and the ability to evaluate organisational positioning, making it suitable for individuals interested in leadership roles or entrepreneurial pathways, regardless of prior experience.

The course delivers a comprehensive and immersive learning experience, combining academic study with practical application. In addition to theoretical knowledge, students engage with real-world business contexts, supported by a 30-week postgraduate professional placement. Students who meet the academic requirements are responsible for securing their own placement, with structured guidance and support provided by the Future Success and Employability Team.

The two-year structure is divided into academic and practical components. The first year focuses on core academic modules, while the second year emphasises the application of knowledge through a professional placement, alongside the development of a reflective portfolio. The final semester also includes modules in Strategic Management Research and Financial Principles and Practice.

Students enrolled on the programme have access to a range of university resources, including the virtual learning environment, StudyNet, which offers access to course materials, peer collaboration, and an extensive collection of e-books and e-journals.

The programme also offers participation in the Young Enterprise Start-Up Programme, delivered in partnership with a leading UK enterprise education charity. Through this initiative, students collaborate in teams to establish and manage real businesses, taking on director-level responsibilities and participating in national and European competitions. This experience is designed to enhance practical skills in innovation, leadership, and entrepreneurship.

Teaching is delivered by research-active academic staff with extensive professional experience. Many are engaged in consultancy and advisory roles with major organisations, including FTSE-listed companies, global health institutions, and innovation-focused enterprises, ensuring that teaching is informed by current industry practice.
4fon:
Studying an MBA can transform the way students think and the way they work, change the way others see them and open up new leadership and management opportunities. This full-time MBA enables students to develop the critical and reflective strategic leadership skills they need to succeed in an uncertain world, challenging their assumptions, cultivating flexible thinking, effective decision making and responsible management.

Hertfordshire MBA students will be supported by first-class facilities, including the virtual learning environment, StudyNet, which provides access to other students, lecture notes and over 100,000 e-books and e-journals. Students will also benefit from teaching and supervision by expert research-active staff, several of whom are world leaders in their field and act as consultants with leading organizations such as Roche, Camelot and BDO Hayward.

At every stage, students will have the opportunity to engage with business, learn through practical, work-based assignments and apply their knowledge in real-world settings in their role. Learners also have the opportunity to undertake a six-month applied business/enterprise experience, where they’ll set up and run their own business or social enterprise. While this supports their learning, they’ll be encouraged to develop and explore their business ideas and apply it directly to their career aspirations.

With an MBA, students can take a life-changing professional journey and expand their mind, skills, career potential and professional network. They can challenge their assumptions and gain a critical, reflexive approach to strategic leadership and management.
9dg1:
The Master of Business Administration with Advanced Project degree is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in business and management, covering key areas such as people management, marketing, and financial proficiency. The programme develops strategic leadership capabilities and the ability to evaluate organisational positioning, making it suitable for individuals from a wide range of academic and professional backgrounds who are interested in leadership roles or entrepreneurial ventures.

Over the two-year course, the first year and the beginning of the second year focus on core academic modules, while the latter part of the second year is dedicated to research skills and an advanced project. This structure enables students to build expertise in project management, analytical thinking, critical thinking, and problem-solving, preparing them for senior roles across diverse business environments.

Students benefit from access to the University of Hertfordshire’s high-quality facilities, including the virtual learning environment, StudyNet, which provides extensive resources such as lecture materials, collaboration tools, and over 100,000 e-books and e-journals.

In addition, students have the opportunity to participate in the Young Enterprise Start-Up Programme, delivered in partnership with a leading UK enterprise education charity. This initiative allows students to work in teams to launch real businesses, take on director-level responsibilities, and compete in national and European competitions, effectively bridging the gap between academic theory and practical experience in leadership, innovation, and entrepreneurship.

Specialization in Data Analytics will allow students to focus on strategic analysis and decision making in the context of the rapidly developing and evolving industry structures, and the uncertain business environment, in which data analytics organizations function.

It examines theoretical and management issues underpinning a wide range of strategic debates relevant to data analytics organizations.
